title: Sum each level of a tree
prompt: Return an array with the sum of the values at each depth of the tree: the root first, then its children, then their children. An empty tree gives an empty array. The supplied tree(value, left, right) builds a node.
hints: How can you know the depth of a node when you reach it?
Carry the depth with each node: the root has depth 0, and a child has its parent's depth plus 1.
Add each node's value to sums[depth], treating a missing entry as 0. Either a queue or recursion works.
checkLabels: The sample tree has sums 8, 13, 21 and 24.
An empty tree gives an empty array.
A single node is one level.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Adds each level on top of the levels above it.

feedback: Label each node of the sample tree with its depth. Each sum is the total of the values that share a label.
